title: Assessing RNA Integrity from FFPE Samples for Spatial Transcriptomics
author: Shuoshuo Wang
materials: silica membrane column-based RNA extraction kit
Spray and clean again using 70% ethanol.

Use a commercial silica membrane column-based RNA extraction kit, for example: RNeasy FFPE Kit (Qiagen), Catalog Number 73504 PureLink FFPE RNA Isolation Kit (Thermo Fisher) High Pure FFPE RNA Micro Kit (Roche) Maxwell RSC RNA FFPE Kit (for automated extraction) Follow the manufacturer's instructions for RNA extraction. Read the "Before start" section from "Guidelines & Warnings" first.

Deparaffinization Preheat a thermal mixer or heat block to 56°C for use. If available, preheat a second thermal mixer or heat block to 80°C to minimize waiting time during the protocol. Do use the blue tinted Daparaffinization Solution (Qiagen #19093) for enhanced visibility of phase separation. Do not use Xylene or organic solvents as replacement due to low flash point and risk of explosion. Home-brew solution can be found in Appendix A of Qiagen RNeasy FFPE Handbook 07/2021
Carefully add 10 µL of Proteinase K, 2mL Qiagen Catalog #19131 to the lower, clear phase.
Discard the collection tube with the flow-through.

Keep RNA samples On ice at all times during the analysis procedure. For quantitation, use a Qubit 4 Fluorometer to measure RNA concentration to determine the appropriate dilution for loading the instrument and gel type. Qubit RNA HS assay has a quantitatie range from 4 to 200 ng. Qubit RNA HS (High Sensitivity) assay Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #Q32852 Pay attention to the quantitative range for : 500-10000 pg/µL for High Sensitivity RNA ScreenTape. So the minimal concentration will be 0.5 ng/uL. The DV200, as a %, might be artificially inflated due to input in the non-quantitative range.​ Do not use NanoDrop for quantitation due to: Inaccuracy: NanoDrop measures sample purity, not the accurate concentration. Low Sensitivity: It is unsuitable for samples with low concentration. The Qubit RNA IQ Assay does not have the necessary sensitivity (>500ng) for small samples. Qubit 4 (Fluorometer, Invitrogen, Q33238)

steps.title: Decontaminate workstation
steps.instruction: Spray all work zones, benches, hoods, pipettes and reagent containers with RNaseZap, RNase AWAY or 0.5 % bleach; wipe with a paper towel treated with the same reagent; rinse surfaces with RNase‑free water and dry.

steps.title: Set microtome and prepare sections
steps.instruction: Set microtome to 10 µm (or 20 µm for less‑collagen samples). Ensure microtome, blades, tools and Eppendorf tubes are RNase‑free, reface the block, discard the first few sections, trim peripheral paraffin and, if paraffin covers >30 % of the section surface, trim the excess.

steps.title: Determine sections and collect
steps.instruction: For ~1 cm tissue use 2 sections; adjust number based on tissue size, cellularity and necrosis (larger or additional scrolls for low‑RNA tissues). Immediately place each scroll into a pre‑labeled, pre‑cooled, RNase‑free microcentrifuge tube; if not processed immediately, store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Add deparaffinization solution
steps.instruction: Add 160 µL Deparaffinization Solution for smaller samples or 320 µL for larger samples. Vortex vigorously for 10 s, then briefly centrifuge to collect the liquid at the tube bottom.

steps.title: First paraffin dissolution
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 56 °C for 3 min to dissolve paraffin.

steps.title: Second deparaffinization vortex and incubation
steps.instruction: Vortex vigorously for 10 s, briefly centrifuge, then incubate again at 56 °C for 3 min.

steps.title: Cool and assess paraffin removal
steps.instruction: Allow the tube to cool to room temperature; if the solution is waxy or solid, add additional Deparaffinization Solution and repeat the 56 °C incubation.

steps.title: Add lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL Buffer PKD (Qiagen #1034963) for smaller samples or 240 µL for larger samples. Mix thoroughly by vortexing.

steps.title: Phase separation centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 11 000 × g (temperature not specified) for 1 min. Mix gently by pipetting up/down; do not vortex.

steps.title: Protein digestion incubations
steps.instruction: Incubate at 56 °C for 15 min, then at 80 °C for 15 min. If only one heat block is available, let the sample sit at room temperature (15–25 °C) while the block reaches 80 °C. Vortex briefly every 3–5 min if the block lacks shaking.

steps.title: Ice incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube on ice for 3 min.

steps.title: High‑speed centrifugation and transfer
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 20 000 × g, 4 °C for 15 min. Carefully transfer the clear supernatant to a new RNase‑free tube, avoiding the pellet of debris and cross‑linked DNA.

steps.title: Add DNase reagents
steps.instruction: Add DNase Booster Buffer equal to 10 % of the total sample volume (≈16 µL) and 10 µL DNase I stock solution to the supernatant.

steps.title: DNase incubation
steps.instruction: Mix by inverting the tube and briefly centrifuge; do not vortex. Incubate at room temperature for 15 min.

steps.title: Prepare Buffer RPE (if new kit)
steps.instruction: Add 44 mL 100 % ethanol to the bottle containing 11 mL Buffer RPE concentrate, mix well, and mark the bottle.

steps.title: Add Buffer RBC and ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 320 µL Buffer RBC to the DNase‑treated sample and mix thoroughly. Then add 720 µL 100 % ethanol and mix by pipetting; do not centrifuge.

steps.title: Load sample onto spin column (first load)
steps.instruction: Transfer 700 µL of the mixture (including any precipitate) to a pre‑labeled spin column in a 2 mL collection tube. Close the lid gently and centrifuge at ≥8 000 × g for 15 s.

steps.title: Load remaining sample
steps.instruction: Repeat the 700 µL loading and 15 s centrifugation until the entire sample has passed through the spin column. Discard each flow‑through and reuse the collection tube; avoid contact with bleach or chlorine‑containing compounds.

steps.title: First wash with Buffer RPE
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Buffer RPE to the spin column, close the lid gently, and centrifuge at ≥8 000 × g for 15 s. Discard the flow‑through and reuse the collection tube.

steps.title: Second wash with Buffer RPE (2 min)
steps.instruction: Add another 500 µL Buffer RPE, close the lid, and centrifuge at ≥8 000 × g for 2 min. Discard the flow‑through and reuse the collection tube.

steps.title: Dry spin column
steps.instruction: Remove the spin column from the collection tube, place it in a new 2 mL collection tube, open the lid and centrifuge at full speed for 5 min to dry the membrane. Ensure at least one empty position between columns and orient lids opposite to rotor rotation to prevent damage.

steps.title: Elute RNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the spin column to a new 1.5 mL tube. Add 14–30 µL RNase‑free water directly onto the membrane, wait 30 s to prime, then centrifuge at full speed for 1 min. The column has a 2 µL dead volume; 14 µL water yields ≈12 µL eluate. Save 4 µL for QC on ice; store remaining RNA at –80 °C.

steps.title: Assess RNA quality (DV200)
steps.instruction: Measure DV200 using a TapeStation (>1 000 pg, High Sensitivity RNA ScreenTape #5067‑5579), BioAnalyzer (>50 pg, RNA 6000 Pico #5067‑1513) or Fragment Analyzer (>100 pg, Agilent DNF‑472 #DNF‑472‑0500) following the manufacturer’s instructions. DV200 <30 % is poor, >50 % is adequate.
